title: Annotatio IV §.I: Institution propositions include a trope — not one that eliminates body and blood
pass_a_gloss: For these words of Christ, uttered concerning the bread taken by Him, blessed, broken, and so given to His disciples, and likewise concerning the cup blessed and offered to the disciples, although on account of the reasons set out in Annotatio I, insofar as they complete a full and entire proposition, they include a Trope and therefore are to be called figurative propositions — the Lutherans themselves by no means wholly denying it, indeed a few explicitly, and all implicitly having to admit the same — yet such a trope as would constitute figurative propositions in that sense which eliminates Christ’s body and blood from the Sacred Supper will be alleged by no Orthodox, Lutherans and Reformed alike.
pass_b_english: Those words (bread taken, blessed, broken, given; cup blessed and offered) do include a trope as full propositions — Annotatio I’s reasons; even Lutherans must admit it, a few explicitly, all implicitly.
But no Orthodox — Lutheran or Reformed — will say the trope is the kind that eliminates Christ’s body and blood from the Sacred Supper.
source_text: Hæc enim verba Christi de pane ab eo accepto, benedicto, fracto, sicque discipulis suis dando, de calice item benedicto similiter, discipulisque porrigendo, enunciata, etsi ob expositas Annotatione Ima rationes, quatenus propositionem plenam ac integram absolvunt, Tropum includant eòque propositiones figuratæ dicendæ sint, non inficiatis omnino vel ipsis Lutheranis, quin paucioribus quidem explicitè, implicitè omnibus idem ipsum admittere necesse habentibus, tamen talem tropum minimè omnium continere eòque sensu figuratas constituere propositiones à quoquam Orthodoxorum, Lutheranorum pariter ac Reformatorum perhibebuntur, quæ corpus & sanguinem Christi Cœnâ S. eliminant.
